significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish both a form-(iii) law—“a teacher model explains worse to novices on topics it knows better”—and a form-(ii) mechanism in which a pre-explanation learner-state representation causally controls explanation level and downstream learning. This would constrain explanations of tutoring failures by predicting a competence–novice-penalty relationship and identifying learner modeling, rather than general linguistic competence, as a causal gate; that distinction bears directly on pedagogical systems such as LearnLM and Tutor CoPilot, which depend on reliable audience adaptation. A verified-false result would distinguishably rule out the proposed expert-blind-spot scaling and internal-mentalizing-gate account, although it would not rule out other mechanisms of audience adaptation; the claim is therefore determinate and both branches are informative. Topic substitution fails: “language and AI intelligence” alone would not warrant this score, whereas the specific scaling relation plus causal learner-model account is substantially more constraining than a median hypothesis on that broad topic.

reach.justification: The named handles are a probe that can “decode the learner's inferred knowledge level ... before it explains,” the “learner-knowledge-level” steering direction, and the predict-then-teach design rule; the probe and rule are ex ante because they operate before an explanation and leave time to alter it. Although the activation direction would require re-extraction on another model, the asserted competence-to-novice-penalty relation and coupling between pre-explanation learner-state accuracy and teaching effectiveness predict what should recur after recalibration rather than merely supplying a search procedure. The hypothesis asserts scope across “several open-weight models and knowledge domains” and hands actionable checks or controls to tutoring, patient-education, and support-system developers who audit or deploy explanations, not only to interpretability researchers. Topic substitution again fails: the broad language–intelligence topic supplies none of these handles, lead time, or cross-domain predictions.
